If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 1–2% in early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecasted price by 1–2% in early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.  
In mid-horizon (8–15 days), if sentiment swings from positive to negative, shift forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per sentiment reversal.  
In late-horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment remains stable above 0.67, apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in mid-horizon to align with sentiment uncertainty.  
If sentiment is mixed and price is trending downward, increase forecast slope by 10–20% in mid-horizon to reflect sentiment drag.
